exposure: mothers who stayed at health facilities before delivery/during conflict
mothers who were satisfied with the healthcare service
mothers who perceived the quality of healthcare favourable
outcome: health system responsiveness (HSR) for intrapartum care
cohort: The participants were 419 mothers who gave birth at health facilities in conflict-affected areas of Wadila, Gayint, and Meket districts in the Amhara region, Ethiopia.
finding: The study revealed that the overall health system responsiveness for intrapartum care in conflict-affected areas was low (45.11%), with mothers in urban areas, government employees, those who stayed at health facilities before delivery/during conflict, those satisfied with healthcare, and those perceiving favorable quality of care reporting higher HSR, while joint decision-making and hospital delivery were negatively associated.
mod_finding: Hospital delivery was negatively associated with health system responsiveness.
cross-section timing: Mothers who gave birth within the last 6 months
